# iothub_device_twin (Resource)

Manages part of a device twin: the tags and desired properties you declare. Reported properties are read-only, in the `iothub_device_twin` data source.

## Ownership

The twin belongs to the device. This resource does not create or delete it. It manages only the innermost keys declared in `tags` and `desired_properties`, leaving other keys untouched. This allows independent resources and systems to share a twin, but writers that manage the same key overwrite one another, including `iothub_configuration` and `iothub_scheduled_job` twin patches.

Omitting a previously managed key removes it from the twin. Destroying the resource removes all of its managed keys. Arrays and empty objects are single values. Omit a key instead of setting it to `null`. After import, the first apply adopts the declared keys without deleting any others.

Keys and values must follow the [twin format rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-device-twins#tags-and-properties-format). JSON formatting, object key order and `2` versus `2.0` do not cause drift.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "iothub_device" "sensor" {
  device_id = "sensor-0001"
}

# Manages exactly these keys: tags.site, tags.fleet.region, tags.fleet.ring,
# desired.telemetryIntervalSec and desired.firmware.channel. The rest of the
# twin is left alone.
resource "iothub_device_twin" "sensor" {
  device_id = iothub_device.sensor.device_id

  tags = jsonencode({
    site  = "munich"
    fleet = { region = "eu", ring = 2 }
  })

  desired_properties = jsonencode({
    telemetryIntervalSec = 60
    firmware             = { channel = "stable" }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device_id` (String) ID of the device. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `desired_properties` (String) The desired properties to manage, as a JSON object (`jsonencode`).
- `tags` (String) The tags to manage, as a JSON object (`jsonencode`).

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) ETag of the twin.
- `id` (String) The device ID. Also the import ID. Every twin resource that manages the same twin has the same `id`.
- `version` (Number) Version of the twin.

## Import

```shell
# Import ID: the device ID.
terraform import iothub_device_twin.sensor sensor-0001
```
